name: Upper Oso Campground (Santa Ynez River)
note: Forest Service campground in Oso Canyon above the Santa Ynez River, off Paradise Road north of Santa Barbara; trailheads for the Santa Cruz Trail and the Aliso National Recreation Trail, and the Camuesa OHV route nearby. Only three sites take a trailer or RV (32 ft). PARTLY OPEN: 10 sites first-come, first-served, the other 14 (mostly equestrian) closed after storm damage (FS, checked 2026-09-24). No drinking water. High river levels can close it in winter. --Claude

name: Tuttletown Recreation Area (New Melones Lake)
note: Bureau of Reclamation recreation area on New Melones Lake near Sonora and Jamestown: about 100 RV sites with 30-65 ft driveways, plus walk-in sites, and a boat ramp. CLOSED: all Tuttletown campgrounds have been closed since a broken pipe took out the area's water supply in 2024; rec.gov shows every site closed through mid-2027 and Reclamation directs campers to Glory Hole (checked 2026-09-24). --Claude

name: Chapman Creek Campground (Tahoe NF)
note: Forest Service campground beside Chapman Creek near the North Yuba River on Highway 49 east of Sierra City (Tahoe NF). 19 RV/trailer sites (published 20-45 ft) plus tent sites; the Chapman Creek Trail starts in camp, the Pacific Crest Trail is nearby, and the Sardine Lakes are five miles away. No hookups or showers; no OHVs in camp. Partly reservable, the rest first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Mecca Flat Campground (Deschutes River)
note: BLM campground on the Deschutes Wild and Scenic River just off Highway 26 north of Madras, 1.6 miles down Mecca Flat Road; the south end of the 7-mile Trout Creek Trail along the river starts here. 13 sites and a group site, first-come, first-served year-round. Vault toilets, no drinking water, no cell. No length is published, but reviewers have brought a 34-ft Class A and 26-30 ft trailers in. The access road is a narrow single lane with a drop-off and few pullouts - reviewers call it bumpy and nerve-racking with a trailer. Goatheads (puncturevine) in the area. --Claude

name: Duncan Reservoir Campground (Silver Lake)
note: BLM campground on small Duncan Reservoir in the sagebrush west of Silver Lake's dry lakebed: 5 miles east of Silver Lake on OR-31, then 5 miles south on gravel County Road 4-14 (sometimes rough, with washouts that reviewers drove around). Four single sites along the west shore, three of them pull-throughs at the water, plus a group site below the dam; boat ramp, covered picnic area, vault toilet, no drinking water, no food or gas nearby. First-come, first-served, open year-round; stocked trout, ice fishing in winter. Open range - watch for cattle. No published site length. --Claude

name: Blanchard Springs Campground (Ozark NF)
note: Forest Service campground in the Blanchard Springs Recreation Area (Ozark NF) north of Mountain View, beside North Sylamore Creek under yellow pines and rock bluffs, near Blanchard Springs Caverns and trout fishing at Mirror Lake. 17 individual sites, all 25 ft - a 23-ft rig fits with little to spare - first-come, first-served, plus reservable group sites. Flush toilets, drinking water and a dump station; no hookups. The campground closes when the creek is high: call 870-757-2211 to check. --Claude

name: Lower Virginia Creek Primitive Campground (Conway Summit)
note: Primitive Forest Service campground at about 9,100 ft in Jeffrey pine off Virginia Lakes Road near Conway Summit, south of Bridgeport: US-395 south 13 miles, right on Virginia Lakes Rd for 2.4 miles, then left on FR 139. The FS says several sites take large trailers or motorhomes. Fire rings, bear boxes, vault toilets; no water, trash service or hookups - pack it out. First-come, first-served, late May to mid-October; fills on summer weekends. A free California campfire permit is required for any fire or stove. --Claude

name: Nineteenmile Campground (Chiwawa River)
note: Small Forest Service campground on the Chiwawa River 22 miles from Lake Wenatchee, reached from US-2 via WA-207 and the Chiwawa River Road (FR 62); the last 10 miles are very rough gravel and dirt that the FS says may not suit low-clearance vehicles. A handful of first-come, first-served sites, trailers to 30 ft; vault toilet, no water. CLOSED: the FS lists it closed by a road washout after the 2026 Little Giant Fire, no reopening date (checked 2026-09-24). --Claude

name: Lower Onion Creek Campground (Colorado River, Moab)
note: BLM campground on the Colorado River off SR-128, 22 miles up the river road from US-191 north of Moab, across from the Fisher Towers turnoff; a river-trip put-in with two boat ramps. 21 first-come, first-served sites (cash or check) plus two reservable group sites; toilets, no water or hookups; 14-night limit. No published length, but reviewers report rigs up to 40 ft and trailers. Minimal cell service. The river has dangerous undercurrents. --Claude

name: Upper Onion Creek Campground (Fisher Towers, Moab)
note: BLM campground on a bench above Onion Creek near the Fisher Towers, 1.5 miles up gravel from SR-128 (22 miles up the Colorado River road from US-191 north of Moab), with red-rock and La Sal views. 14 first-come, first-served sites (cash or check) plus two reservable group sites; toilets, no water or hookups; 14-night limit. Reviewers have brought fifth wheels and Class As of 32-40 ft. The Onion Creek 4WD road starts here - flash floods in the monsoon. --Claude

name: Chalk Bluffs Campground (North Platte River, BLM)
note: BLM campground and boat ramp on the North Platte River east of Alcova: WY-220 east 7.4 miles, then 3.7 miles on County Road 316. Eleven sites with RV parking, tent pads, tables and fire rings, first-come, first-served; vault toilet, no water. A drift-boat launch for the Gray Reef stretch. --Claude

name: Buffaloberry Campground (North Platte River, BLM)
note: Small BLM campground on the North Platte River 12 miles from Alcova: WY-220 east 7.4 miles, then 4.2 miles on County Road 316 (washboard). Four sites with tent pads, tables and fire rings, first-come, first-served; vault toilet, no water. Bank fishing. A reviewer's 23-ft-plus trailer fit, but check the loop before pulling in. --Claude

name: Apgar Campground (Lochsa River, US-12)
note: Small Forest Service campground on a river terrace of giant cedar and fir between US-12 and the Lochsa River (Lochsa Ranger District). About 7 first-come, first-served sites; aggregate roads, vault toilets, tables and fire rings; RVs to 24 ft - a 23-ft rig fits with little to spare. Seasonal, roughly May-September. --Claude

name: Maple Grove Campground (Oneida Narrows Reservoir, BLM)
note: BLM campground (run with PacifiCorp) on the southeast shore of Oneida Narrows Reservoir on the Bear River, north of Preston via ID-34, ID-36 and Oneida Narrows Road, just past Redpoint. 12 first-come, first-served sites, one RV plus one boat trailer or car per site; vault toilets, boat ramp and dock, horseshoe pits; no water or dumpsters. Overnight campers only, 14-day limit. --Claude

name: Battle Creek Campground (Lassen NF, Mineral)
note: Large Forest Service campground on Highway 36 two miles west of Mineral (38 miles east of Red Bluff), close to Lassen Volcanic National Park. 50 sites with grills and tables, potable water, vault toilets; trailers to about 25 ft; open mid-May to September. CLOSED for the 2026 season - the FS says it is unsafe to occupy because of hazardous trees (checked 2026-09-24). --Claude

name: Selby Campground (Carrizo Plain National Monument)
note: BLM campground at the foot of the Caliente Range on the Carrizo Plain National Monument: from Soda Lake Road, 4.5 miles up Selby Road. 13 first-come, first-served sites with tables, fire pits and horse corrals on a packed-gravel loop; accessible vault toilet, three water spigots that may be dry; no garbage service or electricity. Keep rigs to about 25 ft; the monument's dirt roads turn slick and impassable after rain. Spring wildflowers; unreliable cell. --Claude

name: Big Kandiyohi Lake County Park East
note: Kandiyohi County park on the east shore of Big Kandiyohi Lake, 18 miles south of Willmar on County Road 8 (the west unit is a separate park). About 80 electric sites, flush toilets, hot showers, camp store, sandy beach, boat ramp, two camper cabins. May-September; daily and seasonal rates. --Claude  AWH 2026-10-11: the county's ResNexus page showed no availability on any night tried, so no rate could be read; the county opens registration each season, so re-check once 2027 registration opens. --Claude

name: Rosiclare Riverside Campground
note: City of Rosiclare park on the Ohio River in Hardin County, gateway to the Shawnee Hills. 12 water/electric (30/50 amp) sites looking out on the river; dump station, boat ramp, playground. No reservations - call ahead the day you arrive. --Claude

name: E.O. Schultz Park (Elroy)
note: City of Elroy park at the junction of the Elroy-Sparta, 400 and Omaha bike trails. Eight paved RV pads with water and electric, showers, pool next door. First-come first-served, mid-May to mid-October. --Claude

name: Rieck's Lake Park Campground
note: City of Alma park on WI-35 (Great River Road) at Rieck's Lake, a tundra-swan stopover on the Mississippi. 20 paved 20/30-amp electric sites, showers. Tight entrance and sites next to the highway. First-come first-served, April 15-October 15. --Claude

name: Greenwood Park Campground
note: Clark County park on the Black River near Greenwood. About 15 first-come first-served sites with shared electric hookups, water, restrooms (no showers), canoe/kayak put-in. April-October. --Claude

name: Blackhawk Memorial Park
note: Lafayette County park at the Black Hawk War battlefield by Bloody Lake near Woodford. About 35 primitive drive-in sites - no hookups - with water, toilets and boat ramps. First-come first-served (fee envelopes). --Claude

name: Siskiwit Lake Campground
note: Town of Bell campground on Siskiwit Lake near Cornucopia and the Lake Superior shore. Rustic numbered sites, hand-pumped water; hard-sided campers limited to 26 ft. First-come first-served, cash or check. --Claude

name: Loup Park (Lake Babcock)
note: Loup Power District park at Lake Babcock, just north of Columbus. Electric-only gravel pads (big-rig friendly) plus a tent area; potable water in summer, no dump station. First come first served, 7-day limit. May-October. --Claude

name: Wessington Springs City Park Campground
note: City of Wessington Springs campground at the foot of the city park's sledding hill. 13 full-hookup sites (20/30/50 amp), first come first served; pool, playground and tennis courts next door. --Claude

name: Hieb Memorial Park (Marion)
note: City of Marion campground in Hieb Memorial Park by the pond and suspension bridge. Grass sites with electric (15/30 amp) and water, restrooms. First come first served, 14-night max. --Claude

name: Scotland City Campground
note: City of Scotland campground: 6 full-hookup pads (30/50 amp) by the city park with a bath house, and 8 electric-only pads by the ballfields; dump station. First come first served, April-October. --Claude

name: Reeve Lake RV Park (Friona)
note: City of Friona RV park beside Reeve Lake and the community center. About 20 gravel full-hookup pull-throughs (30/50 amp), Wi-Fi. First come first served, pay at City Hall; first night free. --Claude

name: Rhododendron Park Campground (Island County)
note: Island County campground in the woods of Rhododendron Park near Coupeville on Whidbey Island. 15 sites, only 3 of which fit RVs (up to 25 ft); water, portable toilets, no hookups or dump. Reservable. April-September. --Claude  Island County's park page (2026-10-11): 15 pay campsites, 3 of them RV sites with water only (no electric or dump); all first come, first served, no reservations; campground closed October 1 - April 30. --Claude

name: Stanislaus County Fairgrounds RV Park
note: Fairgrounds RV lot in Turlock off Hwy 99. Full hookups (30/50 amp), cash, first-come first-served - call the number on the gate. No showers or other amenities. Year-round. --Claude

name: Lundy Canyon Campground (Mono County)
note: Mono County campground in Lundy Canyon off US-395 north of Lee Vining, along Mill Creek among aspens. 36 sites, most fit rigs to ~35 ft; vault toilets, bear boxes, no drinking water. Cash, first-come first-served. Mid-April to mid-November. --Claude

name: Boulder Creek Campground (South Umpqua River)
note: Small Umpqua NF campground in mixed conifer forest along the South Umpqua River near the mouth of Boulder Creek, 14 miles up paved County Road 46 / FR 28 from Tiller. 7 back-in tent/trailer sites (25-50 ft) with tables and fire rings; vault toilet, no drinking water, no trash service, no hookups. First-come, first-served (scan-and-pay), open year-round. --Claude

name: Island Campground (North Umpqua River)
note: Small Umpqua NF campground right off OR-138 on the North Umpqua River, about 40 miles east of Roseburg. 7 shaded tent/trailer sites with tables and fire rings; maximum trailer length 24 ft, so a 23-ft rig only just fits. Vault toilet, no drinking water, no trash service, no hookups. First-come, first-served (scan-and-pay), open year-round. Highway noise. --Claude

name: Idlewild Campground (Malheur NF, Burns)
note: CCC-built Malheur NF campground in ponderosa pine just off US-395, 17 miles north of Burns (~5,300 ft) - an easy overnight stop that is busy only in fall hunting season. About 24 tent/trailer sites on tight paved loops; the FS says trailers 20 ft and under, but reviewers find 4-5 larger sites that take 25-36 ft rigs (site 1 is paved and roomy) - most sites are short and sloped. Vault toilets, drinking water in summer only, no trash service, no hookups. First-come, first-served, open year-round (Sno-Park permit in winter). Idlewild Loop Trail on site. --Claude

name: Williamson Campground (Lostine River)
note: The largest of the small Wallowa-Whitman NF forest camps along the Wild and Scenic Lostine River, 11 miles up the Lostine River Road (FR 8210, paved then washboard gravel) from Lostine. 8 tent/trailer sites above the road-side bench plus 5 tent-only sites down by the river; reviewers have fit 23- and 31-ft travel trailers. Two vault toilets, no drinking water, no hookups. First-come, first-served, season June-October. No cell service. --Claude

name: Walla Walla Forest Camp (Lostine River)
note: Small Wallowa-Whitman NF forest camp on the Wild and Scenic Lostine River, the first camp above the Lostine Guard Station, about 13 miles up the Lostine River Road (FR 8210) - gravel in good shape to the guard station, rockier beyond. 4 sites with tables and fire rings; sites 1 and 2 are large, and a reviewer fit a 23-ft travel trailer. Vault toilet, no drinking water, no hookups. First-come, first-served, season June-October. No cell service. --Claude

name: Turkey Flat Forest Camp (Lostine River)
note: Tiny Wallowa-Whitman NF forest camp on the Wild and Scenic Lostine River, 16 miles up the Lostine River Road (FR 8210) - rough gravel past the Lostine Guard Station. 3 sites with tables and fire rings; a reviewer fit a 23-ft travel trailer in large site 3, which has wooden steps down to the river. Vault toilet at the entrance, no drinking water, no hookups. First-come, first-served, season June-September. Eagle Cap Wilderness access; no cell service. --Claude

name: New Joe's Campground (Joe's Valley, BLM)
note: BLM campground at the New Joe's bouldering area in Joe's Valley west of Orangeville, on the way up to Joe's Valley Reservoir. 13 back-in sites, 25-50 ft, with tables and deep fire rings; pit toilets, no water, no trash service, no hookups. First-come, first-served, 14-day limit. World-class bouldering; the San Rafael Swell to the east. --Claude

name: Cottonwood Canyon Campground (Joe's Valley, BLM)
note: Small BLM campground in Cottonwood Canyon within the Joe's Valley bouldering area west of Orangeville. 10 sites, driveways 15-30 ft (seven at 25-30 ft, so pick one of those). No hookups. Cash, check or scan-and-pay, first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Pine Campground (Libby Creek, Snowy Range)
note: Small Medicine Bow NF campground in the Libby Creek Recreation Area on Barber Lake Road, just off the Snowy Range Scenic Byway (WY-130) west of Centennial, ~8,600 ft. 6 sites for setups 30-45 ft long; no hookups. First-come, first-served for the 2026 season - pay on arrival by cash or check. Next to Libby Creek Willow; Corner Mountain trails nearby. --Claude
